Params: On the way back to the Wanderer's Lodge, Karenina mumbles incoherently from behind you.
Commandant... I can walk on my own. The way back to... that lodge is pretty far, isn't it?
Don't let this fool you... The Engineering Force... we've had proper training, you know!
In a way, you are glad she was the one who drank the mermaid's tears. Otherwise, having her drag you back would have been pretty rough.
Hey, Teddy... Get me my... wrench...
Hmph, that's not it. You're just doing this... to piss me off... aren't you?
This is kinda... nice. Reminds me of when I was little... Grandpa would carry me home on his back... No matter where I hid...
He would always find me... Mm... I'm really strong now, Grandpa.
Commandant, let's just go ahead with the performance!
When that happens, we'll totally... dazzle everyone, you know? We will, right?
I thought you didn't want to participate.
Hmph, you idiot... You don't get it at all.
When I said I didn't want to go, couldn't you... have... tried a little harder to convince me?
After all... I really wanted to... be with you too... Mmh, it's so hot... Oh, why's it so cold now?
Mm... Why didn't you... ask me about it?
If you'd just asked, I would've... considered it right away!
In the end, you're an idiot, 【kuroname】... and I'm a coward.
Even if I went, I'd probably just... No, I don't want to fail.
Once we're back on the surface, everything will go back to normal. When that happens—
You'll forget all this too, Commandant. Things that aren't real... they'll never be real, no matter what...
Sensing Karenina's mood has dipped because of the performance, you try to come up with a solution...
But she is already fast asleep by the time you have an answer. You hear her steady breathing behind you, and she sounds completely carefree.
The evening breeze stirs her bangs, tickling where they rest against your neck. Her body temperature seems to be running a bit higher than usual.
If it weren't for this place, you'd probably never see her be so open and honest about her feelings.
Yet another memory stirs somewhere deep in Karenina's M.I.N.D., and she remembers something that happened long ago.
Having completed several brutal deadlines, Karenina is yawning incessantly when Bianca arrives with a new flavor of pseudo-caffeine electrolyte solution.
Who would've thought I'd actually gotten used to this stuff lately... This tasteless, bitter drink.
Karenina tips her head back and downs most of the electrolyte drink in one go, musing to herself.
You've been having a bit too much caffeine lately, you know.
Rest is still the best remedy when your M.I.N.D. is exhausted.
There's never enough time! One damn deadline after another... I haven't even finished the old missions, and new ones keep sprouting up like weeds!
Karenina lets herself sink into the pile of books, trying to relax for just a moment.
Oh, I nearly forgot to congratulate you. I heard you're being promoted from demolition team leader to Engineering Force Captain. That's record-breaking time for a promotion.
Karenina looks up, accepting the good news with a calmness she didn't expect. She thought she'd be happier about it, but she isn't.
Hmph... It's not like it was a surprise.
The transfer orders should be coming through soon, but... it still doesn't feel real.
Being captain won't make things any easier. I'll just have more problems to deal with.
Bianca picks up her coffee and takes a small sip, her gaze turning to Karenina with quiet warmth.
I don't worry about you, Karenina.
Learning anything new always comes with growing pains. But once you push through and it becomes second nature, boredom will set in, and you'll start craving the next challenge.
Neither humans nor Constructs can ever be satisfied with the status quo. That restless drive... I suppose that is the essence of life itself.
...Thanks. I'll just take that as a compliment, Bianca.
Sometimes I truly envy that unstoppable drive of yours. No matter the obstacle, it simply shatters the moment it encounters you.
Bianca lowers her voice slightly, her gentle tone carrying an inexplicable edge.
Though... you haven't read that book I lent you recently, have you?
Ngh... That's not true! I read it... I read some of it!
Bianca shifts her gaze from her companion back to the page with an expression of calm insight.
You read a dozen pages before drowsiness kicked in... then you left it sitting on your desk, until you remembered it right before our meeting today.
So you pulled up a summary from the database and skimmed through it hastily. Am I right?
Y-yeah, pretty much. But I think that book's got problems anyway.
Oh? I'd like to hear your take on it.
Mmm... You sure? Fair warning: I haven't read a ton of classics like you have, so don't expect anything profound or eloquent.
That's okay. I just want to hear what you think, Karenina. There's no judgment involved.
I think the protagonist's got problems. She had responsibilities, but she dropped everything and left the moment she got other ideas.
True, she made the wrong choice and crossed the "fence," but I've been thinking... Maybe a life with mistakes is brilliant in its own way.
Many people in this world live and stay within certain boundaries, no matter what... because at least it's safe to live by the book. I call that kind of boundary a "fence."
If she really wanted to change her life because she was dissatisfied, she should've left her situation and found a job...
Bianca can't help but laugh at Karenina's response. After a moment, she composes herself.
Because it's the story of Anna Karenina, not the Engineering Force's Karenina. Given the historical context of that era... No, let's not get sidetracked.
You're right. When faced with different choices, people often ignore what they truly want. They lack the courage to break free from the world they know.
Of course the protagonist made mistakes. Every choice that wasn't safe was a risk.
But even a moth drawn to flame deserves recognition for its courage.
So even knowing it would end in failure, she was still willing to risk it all...
What a strange kind of courage.
That is what literature does. It explores the gray areas of reality... the third option that exists beyond right and wrong.
Morality or laws could certainly be used to label and judge whether people's actions are right or wrong. But when absolute correctness is demanded in fiction, all possibilities are lost.
Both the characters in the story and those reading it must journey inward, searching until they find their answer.
It's okay if you don't understand right now, Karenina. Maybe not understanding it is a kind of virtue in itself.
People feel differently about the same work at different points in their lives. Our experiences shape how we see things.
You really know your stuff when it comes to literature, Bianca...
After all this time, Karenina finally has her answer.
Two Days Until the Songstress Trials
Two Days Until the Songstress Trials\nWanderers' Lodge, Xoth
So yeah, that's the gist of it.
Kiki, having returned at dawn after working through the night, stuffs food into her mouth between breaths.
Hey, Boss, you're looking pretty rough. Were you even listening to what I just said?
Kiki turns to you with a look that says she needs backup.
Did you guys run into some surprise attack I don't know about? Did Karenina beat them up good?
You know, like how she whips us interns into shape.
Her cap pulled down over most of her face, Karenina slumps to the side, muttering under her breath.
If she finds out how much of a lightweight I am, I'm done for!
Oh man... Is Thunder Sparks actually cursed or something? Like, a drunk curse?
I don't wanna end up like Kelly!!!
Deerbear and Huhunina perch on her shoulders, eavesdropping on their master's master's thoughts.
That's the captain for you. Even her battle debriefs are this thorough.
When will I ever be able to hold my own like her?
Pouring Kiki a cup of freshly brewed coffee, you suddenly think that it isn't so bad to have someone idolize you.
Children never realize how chaotic and messy adult lives are.
How's the escape plan coming along?
Calling it "no progress" would be generous. It's bad.
Karenina is still barely conscious, and it seems she won't be recovering from the pseudo-alcoholic electrolyte anytime soon, which means you have to pick up the slack.
Right. Like we discussed before, I started walking in one direction, heading straight regardless of any obstacles I encountered.
No matter which direction I went, it all led back to Lycan Street.
I've been thinking about it... The projection must be covering the entire city and hiding the real exits. By using similar landmarks, they've turned this place into one giant, sealed maze.
Next, I climbed to the top of the tallest tower in the city and used an amplifier to boost my signal range.
But the comms got cut off every time I connected to an external source. There must be some serious signal jammers here.
At least I can confirm that comms within this base is running on a pre-designed point-to-point area network, and not an external one.
Plan B's a wash too, just as expected.
Last but not least, the demolition plan devised by none other than Boss herself!
I waited for the guard shift around dawn to plant the detonators, but the patrol caught me before I was done.
Which is why I got back so late—
They hauled me off to a re-education class and made me read the "Xoth Resident Guide for Temporary Residents" over 80 times, and I couldn't leave until I scored a perfect grade on their test.
All your backup plans have gone down in flames. Security this tight means there must have been tons of escape attempts in the past.
Something is definitely wrong in a city with no exits. Right now, the projection device is still your biggest obstacle.
Actually, there is a Plan D, but...
Karenina has been sitting at the table wrapped in a blanket since the discussion started, but this is the first time she speaks up.
You know what Karenina is thinking, and you know what it will cost her. But you also know she is determined to do it anyway.
Which is exactly why you cannot let her go through with it.
Commandant, you didn't even let me finish!
This plan isn't as dangerous as you think! If we time it right, it can be our fastest way out of here!
No. That isn't even an option.
Nothing is worth that kind of risk.
What are you two even talking about? I'm totally lost here.
Idiot, the projections Xoth uses work directly via your optic nerves.
For humans, the projections will still work even if the organs are damaged, as long as the neural pathways are intact. But for Constructs...
Constructs... Oh! Constructs can control their senses at will!
You want to shut down your visual module and put it offline. Then you can use your sensory module to feel out the base's actual layout!
Absolutely not! I'm with the commandant on this. You know exactly what will happen if you go through with this!
That will only happen if I shut it down for an extended period! Why won't you guys hear me out on this plan?
You have so much to say, but you are arguing against Karenina and her trademark stubbornness. Unexpectedly, Kiki explodes before you can say a word.
No means no! And you're the one who never listens to anyone, Boss!
It's because you're important to us! Why can't you see that?!
If something happens to you, how do I face everyone back home?
And I'm just an intern... I'm not even worth—
Before Kiki can finish, Karenina shoves a piece of bread into her mouth.
Say something that pitiful again, and I'll really get pissed!
Kiki, I never really asked you... why did you come here?
Kiki fidgets with her fingers, her eyes innocent and clear.
There's... something I didn't tell you, Boss.
You know my research is on amplifiers, right?
Of course I do! I might be too busy to make it to every tech meeting, but I read the weekly reports. I know what my team is working on.
I guess I should work on my image within the Engineering Force!
It's physics-based engineering. By adjusting the frequencies, we try to transmit wavelengths at their smallest unit across the maximum possible area.
Think of it like wireless communication. With an amplifier, an area that used to get one bar of signal can jump to receiving five bars.
Truth is, I've been stuck on this research for ages. I can't even convince myself the results are good, let alone good enough to pass the evaluation.
Research doesn't work that fast! Getting all worked up about it won't help!
Pull yourself together, Kiki! And snap out of it already!
Research is all about navigating minefields. Trial and error is the only way to find the right path.
If we wrote off research just because it hasn't produced results yet, there would hardly be any labs in the world.
But the projection amplitude in Xoth is really strong! Boss, didn't you feel it?!
So you think there's research here that aligns with your work!
Yeah, I came here to avoid the evaluation at first. But the moment I arrived and discovered this... I didn't want to leave anymore.
Even if you dock my pay, issue a formal reprimand, or decide you don't want me anymore, Boss... I still want to see that structure with my own eyes.
Even if this whole place gets blown to smithereens, I'll search every inch with a detector until I find it.
I was planning to find the exit, get you and the commandant out safely, then stay behind and keep searching.
That's how selfish I am... I'm causing all this trouble just to stay here, so I don't deserve you doing all this for me, Boss!
Having finally laid bare everything weighing on her heart, Kiki sheds the grown-up facade she's been wearing.
Is that what's been eating you up inside? So what if you wanted to stay?! You think knowing that would've stopped us from coming to get you?!
Idiot... you were more scared of me saying no than getting in trouble, weren't you?
Spiraling in your own head, assuming I wouldn't support you... Kiki, at the end of the day, you don't trust me enough!
Forget about me being your captain or your boss. Ngh... If you respect what we do, you should've been honest with me!
I know, I know all of that, but I would've lost my chance to stay if you'd said no, Boss. I know how selfish and impatient I was being.
A human's life is so short, but my dream feels so impossibly far away... so far that I can't even see the finish line.
Now that she fully understands what Kiki has been thinking, Karenina calms down.
I've known two truly exceptional scientists, both of them human. One was family, and the other... was my teacher!
Their lives weren't any longer than anyone else's, but their dreams reached far beyond.
They accomplished so much in their lifetimes, and we'll accomplish even more. If this is really what you want to go after, I'll support you no matter what.
And if I didn't believe in you, I wouldn't have traveled all this way to find you. Have a little faith in me... and a little faith in yourself!

More and more red text floods your vision, nearly obscuring your entire field of view.
Alright, alright, I get it! I'm going!
You stay here and rest. We'll talk about it when we get back!
Right before she heads out, Karenina hesitates and turns back to add one more thing.
Kiki, it takes a lot of courage to be honest, but it's still better than saying nothing and letting misunderstandings pile up.
Okay, Boss. I... I won't do it again, I promise!
The composer lives in a standalone apartment. Like a grave in a cemetery, the building is unremarkable among the identical structures around it.
After you ring the doorbell, a gentle-looking woman wearing bloodstained rubber gloves answers the door, her smile almost masking the unsettling sight.
You must be the Songstress here for the score, and...
The composer's wife looks at the two of you, words hanging in the air. Karenina lowers her head, hiding whatever emotions flicker across her face.
I'm the composer's wife. My husband is still getting ready, so please, come in. He'll be with you shortly.
The wait is longer than you expected, and Karenina starts browsing the photo wall.
The photos tell the story of the couple: they were childhood sweethearts who got married right after graduation before throwing themselves into their careers.
When a familiar location catches her eye, Karenina pulls you closer to get a better look.
Coffee in the Commercial District, work at the Star of Life, curtain call at a WGAA play... The more details you notice, the deeper the unease you feel.
You look closer. The wife in the most recent photo looks the same as the woman who answered the door, but she looks much younger in the picture.
Meanwhile, her husband has seemingly undergone Construct modification at some point, and it has frozen him at a specific age in the photos... But his smile has faded over time.
If they both served on Babylonia and one of them became a Construct...
